title: Core Hours and Carbon Credits: Incentivizing Sustainability in HPC
problem: HPC users are largely unaware of energy consumption and lack motivation to choose efficient resources; resource provider efficiency efforts miss user-side optimization
motivation: Incentivize user-driven sustainability through energy-aware accounting methods
method: Survey of 300 HPC users on energy awareness; two accounting methods (energy-based and carbon-based charging); simulation and user studies
key_novelty: Demonstration that energy-cost association (not just feedback) drives 40% energy reduction; novel accounting methods for HPC resource charging
contributions: Evidence that only 30% of HPC users are energy-aware
Two novel multi-resource accounting methods (energy and carbon-based)
User study showing 40% energy reduction under cost-based incentives
limitations: User study scope limited to 300 users; accounting method overhead not discussed; long-term behavior change sustainability unclear
